item.title: Political violence: Sowore faults Kukah’s silence, rejects future peace accords
item.description: Human rights activist and the presidential candidate of African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has criticised Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Bishop Matthew Hassan Kukah, over what he described as the silence of his peace committee amid escalating political violence and alleged assassination attempts in the country. Sowore called for the dissolution of the committee, questioning its relevance in the face of repeated attacks on political candidates and their supporters. In a short message sent to Vanguard, the activist said it was time to ask Kukah to shut down his peace committee, accusing it of failing to speak out against violence targeting political actors. He questioned the committee’s silence, asking where it was when candidates and their supporters came under attack. Sowore also declared that he would no longer participate in peace accord signing ceremonies, expressing dissatisfaction with what he considered the committee’s failure to respond to political violence. “For my part, I will never attend another peace accord signing event,” he said. He maintained that peace initiatives should demonstrate commitment to addressing violence and protecting political participants rather than merely organising public signing ceremonies. Oborevwori gave the assurance on Tuesday after meeting with security chiefs over Monday’s violence in Uduere community, where gunmen attacked a campaign gathering involving former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege. While speaking after the meeting, the governor insisted that nobody would be shielded from prosecution on account of their political connections. “We don’t care where they belong to. We don’t care the party. We don’t care about the level of the people who were arrested,” he said. The governor described the incident as unfortunate, saying more than six people had lost their lives. “It’s very sad that we lost over six persons. People know me, I’m not a violent person. And that’s the reason why in my agenda, the fourth pillar of my agenda is to enhance peace and security,” he said. The Nigeria Police Force had earlier confirmed that six people were killed and several others injured in the violence. However, he pointed to an incident from his time as Commander of the Rapid Response Squad in Lagos—when a kidnapped Lagos State Accountant General was being rescued where premature reporting that the suspect had been arrested tipped off the kidnappers’ associates who were demanding ransom, escalating the situation. He cited this as an example of why discretion, relationship-building, and national interest matter at sensitive moments. ​Sharing another experience from his Rapid Response Squad days, he recounted how officers assisting a stranded motorist reacted aggressively when someone appeared with a camera, reflecting officers’ anxieties over past job losses linked to viral footage. item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU), under FCID Alagbon, has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during an intelligence-led raid on an alleged cybercrime hideout, popularly known as a “Yahoo academy,” in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The operation also led to the recovery of suspected fetish materials, including charms, blood-stained items and suspected human remains, alongside 11 iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops and a 2014 Lexus RX 350. The suspects were reportedly arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, following investigations by detectives of the police unit. According to the police, the suspects were allegedly members of an organised internet fraud network known as “Hustle Kingdom”, which operated from the apartment and used the facility as a base for cyber-enabled fraud and other criminal activities. The Police Public Relations Officer of the PSFU, DSP Ovie Ewhubare, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen, saying preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects exploited the identities and personal information of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online. item.title: Champions League: Arsenal face tough Dortmund test as Man City welcome Napoli
item.description: Arsenal will face a stern test when they host Borussia Dortmund in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City welcome Italian champions Napoli to the Etihad Stadium as the competition enters Matchday Five. The two fixtures headline Tuesday’s European action, with both Premier League sides seeking important victories to strengthen their positions in the league phase. Arsenal, who currently occupy third position with 10 points from four matches, will be looking to maintain their impressive European run when they welcome Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium. Mikel Arteta’s side have recorded three victories and a draw in their opening four Champions League matches, beating Napoli, Lille and Slavia Prague before playing out a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich. The Gunners, however, will be without goalkeeper David Raya, who sustained a shoulder injury during their recent encounter with Newcastle United. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are also listed among their unavailable players ahead of the Dortmund clash. Dortmund, meanwhile, arrive in London in good form after moving to the top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 victory over Borussia Monchengladbach at the weekend. The German side have also won three of their four Champions League matches, beating Real Betis, Sabah and Villarreal, although they suffered a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt. They currently sit one point behind Arsenal and will be hoping to close the gap with a positive result in London. The encounter will also offer an interesting reunion for Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri, who is spending the season on loan at Dortmund and is eligible to feature against his parent club. Meanwhile, Manchester City will welcome Napoli in another important encounter at the Etihad Stadium. Enzo Maresca’s side occupy seventh position with nine points, while Napoli are 27th with three points after winning just one of their opening four matches. City head into the fixture after a 1-1 draw against Fulham in the Premier League, having struggled for consistency in recent domestic outings. They will, however, take confidence from their 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig in their previous Champions League fixture as they look to strengthen their chances of securing automatic qualification for the round of 16. City will be without Antoine Semenyo, who is sidelined with a knee injury, while Matheus Nunes remains a doubt. item.title: Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds
item.description: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala. Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round. While Lille are languishing in 35th spot, last season’s semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern’s bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February. But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week’s match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut. That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed. – ‘Own goal’ – In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”, having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season. After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition — and should consider taking a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Rummenigge’s statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen. On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. Kompany, who himself returned on Friday from a month out after being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October, backed Musiala. “The coach must be the one to believe in the player. Musiala has not addressed the controversy directly, but gave an insight into how he shuts out pressure and critique at a fan event this weekend. Asked by a fan how he handled the weight of expectation, Musiala said he was still in the process of finding the right approach. “I’m still learning… Too much pressure isn’t good, but a hunger for victory is important,” Musiala said. “Finding that balance is a very important part of life.” The post Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds appeared first on Vanguard News .

Gaming promotion should not be designed to appeal to under-18s, and adult platforms should have meaningful age-gating rather than a token tick-box. Adults with younger people in their household may also want to use device controls and keep account credentials private. Regulation can involve federal and state-level considerations, so broad claims about legality should always be treated cautiously. The National Lottery Regulatory Commission is a useful starting point for checking official information, while state rules and the status of a particular operator may need separate verification. Before joining a real-money platform, pause and verify A responsible decision begins before an account is opened. It is tempting to judge a platform by its homepage, colour scheme or the number of games listed. Those things tell you very little about the protections behind the service. Check whether you are eligible Real-money gambling is an adult activity. Anyone under 18 should not register or take part. Adults should also confirm that the operator accepts customers in their jurisdiction and that its offering is lawful where they live. Do not assume that a site being visible online means it is authorised for every location. Online access crosses borders easily; regulation does not. Look for a named operator and clear status A credible platform should identify the business running it and provide a route for customer support and complaints. Look for licensing references, but do not stop at a logo or a line of text. Where possible, cross-check the details with the regulator named by the operator. Useful signs to examine include: The company name and registered address. Licence information and the authority said to have issued it. Customer service channels, including how complaints are handled. Rules for identity verification and account restrictions. A responsible-play page that is not buried in tiny footer text. If these basics are difficult to locate, that is information in itself. There is no need to rush. Read terms as if they matter, because they do Terms and conditions often make for dry reading, but they can answer the practical questions that matter most. Check how deposits are processed, which methods are accepted, when account checks may be requested and what happens if there is a dispute. Pay attention to: Any promotional terms, where applicable Transaction limits and processing times Circumstances in which an account may be suspended Rules relating to duplicate accounts Procedures for closing an account The complaint and escalation process A transparent platform should present important conditions in language a normal reader can follow. If the wording is vague, inconsistent or unusually hard to find, take a step back. Treat privacy as part of safety Registration can involve sharing an email address, phone number, payment information and identity documents. That makes privacy policy more than a formality. Read what information is collected, how long it is retained, whether it is shared with third parties and how users can make a data-related request. Nigeria’s Data Protection Act 2023 and the work of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission provide a useful wider context for data rights and obligations. Practical habits help too. Use a unique password, enable available account security features, avoid logging in on public devices and be wary of messages requesting credentials outside the operator’s official channels. Account-control information should be clearly displayed and easy for adults to locate. Responsible play is not a slogan at the bottom of a page. It is a set of controls that should be clear, functional and available before an adult feels they need them. The strongest tools give people a chance to set boundaries in advance. They also make it possible to step away without having to negotiate with customer support. Age gates and identity checks An adult-only service should make its age requirement prominent and use age and identity checks appropriate to its regulatory duties. A simple declaration alone is a weak safeguard. Verification helps protect under-18s and supports the wider integrity of the platform. The exact options vary by operator, but the principle is straightforward: decide the boundary before you are in the middle of using the service. It is worth checking whether reductions take effect immediately and whether increases involve a waiting period. Clear rules reduce confusion. item.title: Questions Linger After Jensen Huang’s Return To Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang’s surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. Is Nvidia in the clear? An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China. US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia’s board that reinstating the company’s cofounder “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP In parallel, the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders. However, the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes might not result in much, Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said. Will Huang be held accountable? Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. The embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees. He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into the company’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures. There are plenty of regulators who are willing to push back against the Trump administration and ask tough questions, Talley said. Trump is also known to flip on people whom he no longer considers friends. “He can become estranged with people, and if that would happen with Jensen Huang, I can imagine a boomerang” on the Trump administration’s approach, Talley said. What does the board’s future look like? The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP Openly opposed to Huang’s return before ultimately reinstating him, the board is in a delicate position. Former Goldman Sachs chief Lloyd Blankfein predicts its days may be numbered. A revolt by shareholders, many of whom supported the reinstatement of the 63-year-old entrepreneur, could reshape the board as soon as 2027, since all directors stand for reappointment every year. If they are spared, the directors could keep Huang on a much “shorter leash” compared to its history of largely deferring to the overwhelming power of this extraordinary executive, Talley said.

item.title: Champions League: Lookman ruled out of Atletico clash, Osimhen’s return uncertain
item.description: Nigerian forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Atletico Madrid’s UEFA Champions League clash against Viking FK, while Victor Osimhen remains doubtful for Galatasaray’s encounter with Aston Villa. The two Super Eagles stars face uncertain fortunes ahead of Matchday Five, with Lookman set to miss Wednesday’s fixture due to injury. According to reports, Lookman will be unavailable when Atletico Madrid face Viking FK on Wednesday, November 25. His absence adds to the Spanish side’s injury concerns, with Marc Pubill and Romero also ruled out. Meanwhile, Osimhen’s availability for Galatasaray’s home encounter against Aston Villa remains uncertain. The striker recently underwent knee surgery after sustaining an injury during Galatasaray’s 2-0 victory over Stuttgart. He resumed individual training on Thursday, November 19, but was not included in the squad for his side’s victory over Samsunspor three days later. His return to action against Aston Villa is therefore not guaranteed. Elsewhere, Moses Usor will be looking to maintain his impressive form for LASK Linz when they travel to face Bodo/Glimt on Tuesday. Samuel Adeniran is expected to lead the attack alongside Usor, who provided an assist in LASK’s hard-fought 2-1 victory over Hartberg on Saturday. LASK currently occupy 16th position with six points and will be hoping to improve their standing with a positive result in Norway. On Wednesday, fellow Nigerians Mubarak Suleiman and Emmanuel Ayaosi are expected to feature when Slavia Prague host Villarreal at the Fortuna Arena. Slavia have endured a difficult campaign, sitting 34th with just one point after four matches. They are yet to record a victory in the competition. Another Nigerian youngster, Christian Nwachukwu, could also feature when Sabah host Spanish giants Barcelona at the Baku Olympic Stadium on Wednesday. The 20-year-old joined the Azerbaijani club from Sheffield United in August and will have an opportunity to test himself against one of Europe’s biggest sides. item.title: Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked. Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.” Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.” “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days. With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact. “Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.” The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed. “I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois. He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain. “Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said. Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August. Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States. Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.” Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.” “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days. With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact. “Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.” The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed. “I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois. He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain. “Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said. Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August. Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States. item.title: Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the incident, including the actions of police officers deployed to the venue. CSP Ani Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that preliminary police findings indicated that six people were killed. “Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement read. Iniedu said the IGP had instructed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. He added that the probe would examine the sequence of events, establish the identities of those involved and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the actions and deployment of police personnel at the scene. The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. “In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” the statement read. The police urged residents, community leaders, political stakeholders and campaign groups to remain peaceful, obey the curfew and refrain from circulating unverified reports that could worsen tensions. It also called on anyone with useful information, photographs, video footage or other evidence to assist the investigation by submitting them through established police channels, assuring that the identity of informants would be protected. The police confirmation followed an earlier allegation by the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour of the area. The organisation had put the death toll at four, including two of its aides, identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while claiming that four other people sustained critical injuries. item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.

item.title: ‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠⁠​​‌⁠‌INEC to conduct mock accreditation in 490 Lagos polling units
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 490 polling units across Lagos State on Saturday. Prof. Ayobami Salami, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Lagos. Salami said the exercise would take place between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. in selected polling units across the state. He said it was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify possible gaps or challenges that would be addressed before the 2027 general elections. According to him, the exercise will cover the 245 Registration Areas (RAs) across the state’s 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs), with two polling units selected in each Registration Area. He urged residents, particularly eligible voters in the selected polling units, to participate in the exercise to enable the commission to assess the effectiveness of its equipment and electoral processes. The REC said the list of selected polling units would be displayed at the respective local government area offices to enable residents to identify the designated locations. Salami said he had directed all electoral officers in the state to convene stakeholder meetings in their respective LGAs ahead of the exercise. He said the meetings would provide an opportunity to engage political parties and other stakeholders on the importance of participating in the mock accreditation exercise. The REC said the engagements would also help mobilise eligible voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise. He outlined the activities preceding the exercise, saying BVAS configuration would take place on Nov. 25, followed by the training of nominated personnel on Nov. 26. According to him, personnel and devices would be deployed to the selected polling units on Friday, ahead of the exercise. Salami reiterated that the exercise formed part of INEC’s preparations to ensure a smooth and efficient electoral process during the 2027 general elections. item.title: Woman attacks police inspector, tears uniform during arrest
item.description: By Steve Oko A woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, has been arrested by the Abia State Police Command for allegedly assaulting a police inspector and tearing his uniform during a confrontation in Aba. The suspect was also accused of attacking worshippers with fireworks at Christ the King Church (CKC), Aba, triggering panic within the church premises. The police said Barkerk was arrested on Sunday, November 22, after a distress call alerted the Ndiegoro Divisional Police Headquarters to an attack on church members by hoodlums throwing explosive fireworks indiscriminately. According to the Command, a patrol team deployed to the scene to restore order apprehended the suspect with fireworks in her possession. However, she allegedly turned violent, assaulted an inspector attached to the patrol team, tore his uniform and attempted to forcefully retrieve the recovered exhibits. The police said she was subsequently subdued and arrested, while the fireworks and other relevant exhibits were secured for investigation. The Command’s spokesperson, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this in a statement Monday, condemning the assault as reprehensible and warning against attacks on officers performing lawful duties. She said the suspect would be charged in court after investigation. Chinaka added that normalcy had been restored at the church and its environs, while police monitoring continued to prevent further breakdown of law and order. The Command warned that it would not tolerate assault, obstruction or interference with police officers in the discharge of their duties, urging residents to maintain peace and respect lawful authority. item.title: YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings
item.description: Ms Rachel, the American creator of hit sing-songy educational videos for toddlers, attacked the use of immigration hearings for children following a courthouse visit on Monday. “I’ve seen children who are just missing the light in their eyes and they’re begging to go to the spelling bee or to just, you know, be with their younger siblings,” said Ms Rachel, who is known offline as Rachel Accurso. “They’re just so scared and praying to God, that they, please change the hearts of ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) and let us out,” added the 43-year-old after observing legal procedures of juveniles being processed through the immigration courts. Her appearance at the New York youth immigration court was part of an effort to shine light on the Trump administration’s immigration policy that was supported by newly elected US lawmaker Brad Lander. Lander criticized a “travesty of justice” as cases are sped up while funding for legal representation is cut. In videos uploaded to her 22 million subscribers on YouTube, Ms Rachel, known for her signature pink headband and denim overalls, teaches infants to identify animals, colors, and numbers. On her other social media platforms, she is taking an increasingly vocal stand for children’s rights. She has notably led a fundraiser for the organization Save the Children in support of Palestinian children in Gaza and has backed campaigns critical of US migrant detention centers where children are kept, decrying poor conditions and calling for their closure. Targeted by a smear campaign for her pro-Gaza stance, Ms Rachel said previously that it would be more controversial to say nothing. “I think it’s sad to take someone’s dedication and love for all children and try and make that wrong,” she told PBS last year. item.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder diagnosis
item.description: Former world heavyweight boxing champion, Tyson Fury, has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a forthcoming Netflix documentary about his life and career. According to Deadline , Fury made the revelation in the feature-length documentary titled Tyson Fury , which is scheduled for release later this month. The boxer said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after defeating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 to become the world heavyweight champion. He also disclosed that he received a bipolar disorder diagnosis in 2017. Reflecting on his mental health struggles in the documentary, Fury described experiencing periods of severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much,” he reportedly said. Fury also recounted experiencing intense anxiety that frequently woke him in the middle of the night. He said he eventually sought professional help from a psychiatrist in London, who assessed him through a series of questions and identified depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. The documentary also features contributions from his wife, Paris Fury, and father, John Fury, who discuss his mental health challenges. item.title: Nigerians Firmly Behind APC Despite Criticism And Insults — Yari
item.description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, has said the massive turnout at the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State demonstrates the people’s acceptance of the party despite what he described as campaigns of calumny and insults against it. Yari said the APC was consolidating its support base to secure victory at all levels in the 2027 general elections, attributing the party’s growing acceptance to its closeness to the masses. He stated this on Monday during the APC campaign flag-off held in Talata-Mafara, which attracted party faithful, support groups and members of the public. All Progressives Congress governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State on Monday, November 23, 2026. Crowds of party supporters welcomed Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara town before proceeding to the town’s Eid ground, venue of the rally. Speaking at the event, Senator Yari said the large turnout reflected the enthusiasm and commitment of party members and supporters towards the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party,” he said. The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, and Governor Radda Dikko during the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State, on Monday, November 23, 2026. Also speaking, Governor Dauda Lawal expressed gratitude to party supporters for their show of solidarity, while commending the people for their resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence. He reaffirmed his administration’s resolve to promote inclusive governance, equitable development and sustained engagement with communities across the state. “This crowd speaks for itself; there is very little to say other than to thank Almighty God. Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude. “At this point, I will simply say, let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day,” Lawal said. The APC campaign train is expected to move to other local government areas of Zamfara State as the party intensifies its mobilisation and grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA launches nighttime evacuation gangs
item.description: …Plans over 10 regional offices ahead of Yuletide By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) has launched a nighttime waste evacuation operation across the state to tackle mounting refuse heaps and restore environmental sanitation ahead of the Christmas and New Year festivities. The exercise, which commenced on Monday night, began along the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, with sanitation teams and heavy-duty equipment deployed to clear identified waste black spots. LAWMA’s Acting Managing Director, Olajuwon Akinyemi, led the operation at Igando Bus Stop alongside the Acting Executive Director of Operations, Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director of Finance, Kunle Adebiyi. Speaking during the exercise, Akinyemi said the nighttime evacuation would be extended to other major entry routes and high-traffic corridors, including Ojota–Ikorodu Road, Mushin–Moshalashi axis and Lekki–Ajah corridor. He said the operation was aimed at restoring Lagos’s environmental appeal and providing a cleaner and healthier atmosphere for residents and visitors expected in the state during the busy December holiday season. To prevent cleared locations from becoming refuse dumps again, the agency said it was partnering with traditional institutions across the state to strengthen community monitoring and enforcement. Beyond the immediate clean-up exercise, Akinyemi announced plans to establish more than 10 regional offices across Lagos as part of efforts to decentralise the authority’s operations. He described the restructuring as non-negotiable, saying the regional offices would improve operational coordination, bring waste management services closer to communities, strengthen accountability and ensure faster responses to sanitation challenges. The LAWMA boss appealed to residents to remain patient with the state government as it works to address waste management challenges across the metropolis. He also urged residents to promptly report service failures by Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators through the authority’s official communication channels to enable it to enforce compliance. item.title: Omo Agege attack: ‘Enough is enough’, arrest, prosecute perpetrators – Keyamo tells police
item.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible. Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment. He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery. The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice. “I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said. Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings. “Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said. He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence. The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere. “Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said. Keyamo maintained that only law enforcement agencies had the authority to deal with offenders, warning political leaders against encouraging their supporters to attack other citizens. He described such conduct as a sign of desperation and called on the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address residents and warn those threatening violence. “I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone. “Enough is enough,” he said. item.title: Fani-Kayode denies recall, meets Enikanolaiye
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has denied reports that he was recalled from his diplomatic posting, saying his visit to Abuja was to brief the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on his activities and consult with officials. Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting with the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. He said the meeting was part of his official responsibilities and had nothing to do with reports circulating on social media that he had been recalled. “There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue. “If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister,” he said. The envoy explained that his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa. He said he had initially planned to spend only a few days in South Africa following his posting but had extended his stay to complete necessary diplomatic procedures. Fani-Kayode also dismissed reports that his meeting with South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) over the controversy surrounding the omission of his speech during the presentation of his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa amounted to a reprimand. He described the engagement as cordial and constructive, saying concerns were addressed professionally by both sides. “Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said. The high commissioner reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, particularly in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest. “I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent.
